It uses a Necurs DGA session to surface related malicious domains tied to Facebook-linked campaigns that reportedly installed a malicious browser extension. It also notes a spike of JS-hosting domains under one top-level domain and a registrant account whose domains were blocked. No threat actor is named.

05d460230449630e5d22e7edcd53265a4b421c45.summary: Blog post by cocomelonc, published 2026-06-23, describing macOS persistence through Folder Actions: an AppleScript attached to a folder runs a harmless C program when files are added. It is presented as a safe lab proof of concept that writes a log file, with notes on GUI and command-line registration, cleanup, and blue-team detection hints. No threat actor, campaign, sector, country or CVE is named.

052b7ca5936790e7f589583cd30e9ceb3d8a040c.summary: This is a vendor marketing page for ThreatConnect's automated phishing analysis and response platform. It describes product features such as email analysis, playbooks, prioritisation and user reporting, and includes a customer testimonial and a request for a product demo. It does not describe any threat actor, campaign, malware, vulnerability or incident, so it is not a threat report and no facts are recorded.

05afe2ddb7ee4ca32988e7f841d182f25d862c41.summary: Computer Weekly reports that US authorities announced charges against three alleged members of the Carbanak gang, also known as Fin7 and JokerStash, believed responsible for over 100 cyber heists. The gang is said to have targeted banks in more than 40 countries, using Carbanak and Cobalt malware and deceptive emails to steal payment card data. Europol cites cumulative losses above €1bn. Two suspects were in custody awaiting extradition, and one had been arrested in Germany in January.
